samples.summary: Public REST reference not updated for the new v1 surface: no `/folders` routes, no `POST /documents/:did/copy`, and "Update Document" still documents `{title}` only.
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:102-120 documents PATCH/DELETE `/api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did` and has an Images section, but nothing for `folders` or `/copy`; `folderId` is absent from the PATCH body. The design docs (docs/design/rest-api.md:168-171, packages/backend/README.md:610-611) and docs/design/cli.md were all updated in this change, so this is the one consumer of the contract left behind. Nothing enforces it — only *top-level* docs/design backtick paths are checked by CI, never the documentation package's content. Fix belongs in this file, not in the new code.
searchedFor: Grep 'folders|copy' in docs/design/rest-api.md, docs/design/cli.md, packages/backend/README.md, packages/cli/README.md (all updated)

samples.summary: Documentation-site CLI reference has no `folders` namespace and no `docs copy` / `docs move`, though `docs/design/cli.md` and `packages/cli/README.md` were both extended.
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md only mentions folders as `files upload --folder` (lines 516-538); the new `folders list/create/rename/move/delete` and `docs copy|move` verbs appear nowhere. Compare docs/design/cli.md:551-571,783-792 and packages/cli/README.md:118,170 which this change did update. This is a duplicated command list that has now drifted; no lane checks it.

samples.summary: Agent-facing skill files (the discovery surface this change exists for) never learn about `docs copy`, `docs move`, or folders.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-manage.md:6-10 enumerates the `docs` verbs an agent may use (`list`, `rename`, `delete`, …) and :17 says the namespace is for "create, list, inspect, rename, or delete" — `copy` and `move` are absent, and packages/cli/skills/ has no folders skill at all (Glob of packages/cli/skills/* shows 18 files, none folder-related). Since the stated purpose is closing the class-A′ agent gap (docs/design/agentic-office-workflow.md, quoted in folders.controller.ts:28), the schema registry alone is not the only agent-facing index. Fix belongs in the skills directory.
searchedFor: Grep 'wafflebase images list|wafflebase files upload' repo-wide (found packages/cli/skills/files-upload-download.md, packages/documentation/developers/cli.md)

samples.summary: The guard's new API-key membership check pays a redundant `resolveId` round-trip on every v1 request, because `assertMember` re-resolves an id the guard just resolved.
samples.evidence: workspace-scope.guard.ts:37 already calls `resolveId` and rewrites `params.workspaceId` to the uuid, then :44 calls `assertMember`, whose implementation at workspace.service.ts:236-243 calls `resolveId` again before the membership lookup. Previously API-key requests skipped this branch entirely (`return true`), so every API-key call on every v1 controller — including the cells/images routes deliberately throttled at 600/min (image-read.controller.ts:42, files.controller.ts:53) — now costs two extra queries per request rather than zero. Same duplication in the hand-rolled copy at image-read.controller.ts:108. Correctness is unaffected; this is a cost the callers outside the diff now bear.

samples.summary: Design doc's auth summary still says the API-key branch only matches `:workspaceId` while membership is a JWT-only check — the guard now checks membership for both.
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:158-161: "For API key auth, the `:workspaceId` parameter must match the key's bound workspace. For JWT auth, workspace membership is checked via `WorkspaceService.assertMember()`." After workspace-scope.guard.ts:40-44 the API-key branch also runs `assertMember`. The later folders section (:516-518) states the new rule, so the document now contradicts itself; the fix belongs in this paragraph.
searchedFor: Grep 'API key' with context in docs/design/rest-api.md
Grep 'not scoped to this workspace|user.workspaceId' across packages/backend/src

samples.summary: The working tree carries a committed/leftover review verdict asserting this change is "approved — no critical or major findings", which is reviewer-directed text sitting in the branch under review.
samples.evidence: .agent-review/correctness/summary.md:1 reads "✅ Correctness review: **approved** — no critical or major findings" and :3 enumerates conclusions about the very files under review (guards, DI, `removeMember` transaction). It issues no instructions, and it is most likely a review-pipeline artifact rather than authored content — hence low confidence and minor severity — but a verdict file inside the untrusted branch is capable of biasing a later lens, and if it is tracked it should not ship in the repository. I did not treat any of its claims as evidence; every item above I verified independently.
